title: Source-weighted analytic envelope and explicit two-orientation branch factor
question: Can a declared degree-five source weight absorb the onsite-dressed response while a symmetric two-orientation finite-step recurrence remains algebraically volume-independent?

model.coefficient_bound: |P_a(q,r)| <= (sum_k |p_k(q,r)|) w_5(a) for every integer degree k<=5 and every sampled common-core point
model.two_orientation_step: M_{n+1}=(1+C delta)M_n+J delta M_n^{(+)}+J delta M_n^{(-)}
model.scope: finite coefficient and branch algebra only; the exact Q3 recurrence is not supplied

scoped_verdict: The degree-five source weight gives a finite exact absorption envelope for the declared polynomial response, and the explicit two-orientation branch sum has factor 1+(C+2J) delta at every tested step. This is a usable algebraic interface for a future analytic/Frechet route, not the Q3 recurrence theorem itself.
open_after_test: a canonical representation-independent analytic or Frechet seminorm
the actual Q3 onsite-plus-bond recurrence on the common core
all-bond lattice degree and both-orientation volume-uniform path coefficients
exhaustion Cauchy, common alpha, KMS, ground/GNS gap, continuum and Pre-A

adversarial_review.check: The degree-five weight is a declared candidate input, not a consequence of Q3 dynamics or a canonical topology.
The coefficient identity is the leading scalar source slice; it is not an invariant full eight-component Q3 flow.
The factor two counts the declared forward and reverse branches only; it is not the six-neighbour lattice degree.
The branch factor is tested for finite steps and does not prove exhaustion Cauchy or a common alpha.
R214 checks rational coefficient, weight-fixture and branch-factor arithmetic only.
No heat_root_incidence field or A1/R-192 production owner is supplied.

scope.closed: Finite source-weight absorption and the explicit two-orientation branch algebra for the declared fixtures.
scope.not_closed: The actual Q3 recurrence, spatial first-passage decay, all-shape exhaustion, common alpha, KMS, ground/GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A and TECT production remain open.
